candidates.evidence: NASA’s Ceres facts page states that Ceres completes one rotation every 9 hours, so the duration is 32,400 seconds.
candidates.familiarity: Ceres is a commonly taught dwarf planet/asteroid-belt object, and a “day length” is an intuitive school-science comparison.

candidates.evidence: NASA’s Neptune facts page says one day on Neptune takes about 16 hours, which converts to about 57,600 seconds.
candidates.familiarity: Neptune is one of the eight planets students learn, and comparing planetary day lengths is a familiar space-facts topic.

candidates.evidence: NASA’s Sun facts page states that the Sun rotates once every 25 Earth days at the equator, which is 2,160,000 seconds.
candidates.familiarity: The Sun is universally familiar, and many people know it rotates even though it is not solid like Earth.

candidates.evidence: Hasbro’s BOGGLE 04601 page says players search for words while a 3-minute timer counts down, so the duration is 180 seconds.
candidates.familiarity: Boggle is a long-running word game commonly played by families, in classrooms, and by casual board-game fans.

candidates.evidence: The ICC 2025 playing conditions specify one scheduled drinks interval of 2 minutes 30 seconds at the midpoint of each innings, giving 150 seconds.
candidates.familiarity: Cricket is one of the world’s most-followed sports, and a short drinks break is easy for players to picture even if they do not know the exact value.

source.name: ICC U19 Women’s T20 World Cup 2025 Playing Conditions

candidates.evidence: World Rugby’s 2025 laws say a conversion kick must be taken within 60 seconds from when the try was awarded.
candidates.familiarity: Rugby is a widely watched international sport, and the post-try conversion is one of its most recognizable moments.

source.name: World Rugby Laws of the Game 2025
